findings.title: Entry meter is per-thread: a threaded re-entry inside a patched _execute is neither counted nor refused, yielding a verified receipt with I_executed=1 for two real entries
findings.steps: orig_exec=CompoundMachine._execute; orig_adv=CompoundMachine.advance; done=[]; def p(self,*a,**k): r=orig_exec(self,*a,**k); (not done) and (done.append(1), (t:=threading.Thread(target=orig_adv,args=(self,),kwargs={'allow_acquisition':True})).start(), t.join()); return r; monkeypatch CompoundMachine._execute=p; receipt=execute_grant(machine, grant_for(machine, calls=1, allow_acquisition=True)). Expected under HARNESS_SPEC ('refuses an unexpected second entry'): InvalidNativeObservation. Actual: sys.setprofile applies only to the calling thread, so the 'call' event for the second advance is never seen -> invoked=1, entry_refused=False, prefix/chain/budget checks pass (both events are genuine, chained), receipt returned with I_executed=1, native_event_count covering two advances, verify_receipt True. Stdlib probe (scratchpad/probe_setprofile.py case C) confirms invoked=1/refused=False with 2 real entries on both 3.11.15 and 3.12.3. Same threat class as the in-scope test test_internal_reentry_that_clears_meter_never_publishes_a_count (patched _execute re-entry); requires no hook change and no native-object mutation, so it is not obviously excluded by the stated trust model. Hardening: install threading.setprofile(entry_meter) for the window (and clear it), and/or refuse when threading.active_count() changed during the call, or narrow the HARNESS_SPEC/CONTRACTS claim to same-thread entries. Downgrade to NOTE only if the owner rules in-process patching of the pinned class out of scope.

findings.title: Hook-clearing re-entry (sys.setprofile(None) inside patched _execute) is undetected; explicitly outside trust model but a one-line check exists
findings.steps: Patched _execute calls sys.setprofile(None) then orig_adv(self) -> invoked stays 1, entry_refused False, receipt published. In the finally block, checking `if sys.getprofile() is not entry_meter: entry_refused = True` before clearing would catch both this and the exception-cleared case at no cost.

findings.title: I_attempted is unconstrained by verify_receipt
findings.steps: I_attempted is always int(calls and actuator_enabled) at HEAD (the only attempted=1/executed=0 path is sys.setprofile raising inside the try, which yields a NativeStepFailed receipt). A re-digested I_attempted=5 passes verify_receipt; spec only constrains I_executed/I_allocated, so no wrong outcome, but the field carries no integrity beyond the digest.

findings.title: control.py discards the adapter-level digest; only the control-level digest survives
findings.steps: receipt.pop('receipt_digest') then re-digest after adding I_predicted/board fields. verify_receipt still holds (counters untouched, canonical JSON sorts keys), and replay verifies every control receipt against the caller-held bundle digest. The adapter's own digest is not retained inside the control receipt, so a control receipt cannot be traced to the adapter output independently - integrity only, as CONTRACTS.receipt_integrity already states.

findings.title: verify_receipt does not cross-check counters against events
findings.steps: A re-digested receipt with I_executed=0 and non-empty native_event_refs passes verify_receipt; replay's OBSERVATION_EVENT_COVERAGE_MISMATCH and the caller-held bundle digest catch it end-to-end, so no concrete wrong outcome.

findings.title: Chain anchor is machine-private, not external
findings.steps: Mutating records AND rewriting the last trace event (post_state_hash, recomputed event_hash) AND trace_head passes result() because the chain is anchored only at _episodes[-1].initial_state_hash held by the machine. Explicitly outside the trust model (mutates native objects); replay is anchored by the caller-held bundle/journal digests and catches it there.

py311_hazards: No behavioural difference found between 3.11.15 and 3.12.3 for the semantics the meter relies on: a profile-callback exception clears the profile and propagates; frame.f_locals['self'] is readable at the 'call' event; bound-method identity checks; settrace coexistence (scratchpad/probe_setprofile.py, both interpreters).
Local lead runs used 3.11.15 while aws_validation/worker.py:64 enforces 3.12 (PYTHON_312_REQUIRED); the three NameError failures are interpreter-independent and will reproduce on 3.12.

3.12: sys.setprofile is implemented over sys.monitoring; the sys.getprofile() precheck (adapter L295) cannot see sys.monitoring tools (e.g. coverage's sysmon core) but they do not disturb the meter; setprofile also succeeds when PROFILER_ID is already claimed (probe E/F). No refusal misfires; no hazard.

Syntax/API used (str.removesuffix 3.9+, dataclass slots=True 3.10+, runtime kw_only 3.10+, datetime.timezone.utc) is valid on both. 3.13's PEP 667 f_locals proxy still supports .get - irrelevant for the 3.12 pin.
Test-side: aws_validation/test_launch_transport requires boto3/botocore (2 failures in the first local run without them); the 61-test gate depends on the pinned wheelhouse, not on the adapter.
verdict_basis: All three items are implemented at HEAD and the implementation matches HARNESS_SPEC/CONTRACTS on inspection, but 3 of the 61 predeclared cases - the dedicated regression tests for items 1 and 3 - fail with NameError (missing module-level `from cncm.model import TerminalStatus` in test_native_step_adapter.py), reproduced in two local runs at aa600668. The acceptance boundary (all cases must run and pass on the frozen Lane-A source) cannot be met, and the resealed-state rule has no executable coverage. Additionally the per-thread entry meter can be bypassed by a threaded re-entry from a patched _execute (MAJOR, trust-model-dependent). Fix is small: one import line, optional threading.setprofile/getprofile hardening, rename shadowed variable. Corroboration: with only that import added, a sibling run shows 61/61 passing (wt_patch_pytest.xml).
corroboration: Sibling worker's patched run (scratchpad/PATCH_test_native_step_adapter_import.diff adds `from cncm.model import TerminalStatus` at module scope; scratchpad/wt_patch_pytest.xml): 61 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, including test_no_frame_has_no_return_identity_before_during_and_after_root_call and test_work_join_refuses_records_removed_from_trace_bound_state[False|True]. So once executable, the item-1 and item-3 regression tests pass against HEAD's adapter; the defect is confined to the test module's import, not the adapter logic.
